excerpt: BrowserStack is a cloud testing platform for websites and apps on real browsers and devices. Founded in 2011; Live plans from USD 29/month billed annually.
content:
BrowserStack lets developers and QA teams test websites and mobile apps on real browsers and real iOS and Android devices in the cloud, instead of keeping their own device lab. Its products include Live (manual cross-browser testing), Automate (running Selenium, Playwright and other automated tests in the cloud), app testing, visual testing, accessibility testing and test management, and it now advertises a set of AI agents for testing work. Its company page cites 3,500+ real devices and browsers, 21 data centres and more than 50,000 customers in 135+ countries.

BrowserStack's company page says Ritesh Arora (cofounder and CEO) and Nakul Aggarwal (cofounder and CTO) founded it in 2011. Its June 2021 press release announced a USD 200 million Series B at a USD 4 billion valuation, led by BOND with Insight Partners and existing investor Accel, and described the company as profitable since its inception. It had earlier raised a USD 50 million Series A from Accel in 2018.

Prices are published. On 15 October 2026 the pricing page listed Live Desktop at USD 29 a month and Live Desktop & Mobile at USD 39 a month for a single user, and Automate from USD 59 a month (Chrome Desktop), all billed annually; a Freelancer plan costs USD 19 month-to-month or USD 12.50 a month billed annually. Team, enterprise and volume plans cost more or are quoted.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product for this page, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.summary_short: Cloud testing on real browsers and devices: manual, automated, visual and accessibility testing

use_cases: Checking a website on Safari, Chrome, Edge and Firefox across operating systems
Testing a mobile app on real iPhones and Android phones
Running automated Selenium or Playwright suites in parallel from CI
Catching visual regressions and accessibility issues

fit: ship websites or apps that must work across many browsers and devices
want to run automated tests in parallel without maintaining a device lab
need published per-user prices to budget
not_fit: only test on one browser you already have
need a permanently free tier for ongoing use

Costs rise quickly with parallel automated tests
